battle.name: 奧地利內戰
battle.brief: 奧地利內戰於1933年二月爆發，聯邦政府軍與社護團等反政府武裝在維也納及施蒂利亞交火，衝突延續至1934年。線膛砲（Muzzle-loading field gun，1850年）為德國陸軍沿用的野戰火炮型號，可與步兵協同作戰。

kit.name: 線膛砲
kit.history: 線膛砲是德國陸軍早期野戰砲兵的一類裝備，配置於步兵支隊以提供支援火力，並與其他野戰砲共同構成軍隊的砲兵層級。

countries: 這是一場發生於奧地利共和國境內的內戰，主要戰場集中在維也納與多瑙運河兩岸；下奧地利的維也納新城、上奧地利與施蒂利亞的礦區及鐵路據點也出現短暫武裝響應。政府一方由聯邦陸軍、聯邦警察與受政府扶植的海姆韋爾武裝組織構成；起義一方以與社會民主黨關係密切的共和國防護團、地方社會民主黨組織及其武裝戰鬥員為核心，共產黨員亦有參與，卻沒有另建能與維也納主力協同的獨立縱隊。外國沒有以正規部隊投入交戰，起義者所獲外援也不足以形成外部戰場。從開始便由政府控制內城、國家電台與主要兵營，起義者則先靠奪取武器，在城市外圍建立據點。
countriesEn: This was a civil war within the Republic of Austria. Its principal fighting was concentrated in Vienna and on both banks of the Danube Canal; short-lived armed responses also occurred in Wiener Neustadt in Lower Austria and in mining and railway points in Upper Austria and Styria. The government side consisted of the Federal Army, federal police, and the government-backed Heimwehr paramilitary organization. The insurgent side was centered on the Republikanischer Schutzbund, which was closely tied to the Social Democratic Party, together with local Social Democratic organizations and their armed fighters. Communists also took part, but they did not create an independent column capable of coordinating with the main force in Vienna. No foreign regular forces entered the fighting, and outside assistance to the insurgents was insufficient to create an external battlefield. From the outset, the government held the inner city, the state radio service, and the main barracks, while the insurgents first obtained weapons and established positions on the city's outskirts.
cause: 1933年的經濟蕭條、失業增加與工資削減，使勞資衝突重新升高。1927年的社會民主黨武裝起義遭鎮壓後，該黨失去執政機會，其合法政治空間與武裝骨幹也受到限制；多爾福斯政府則依靠基督社會黨、聯邦警察及海姆韋爾，逐步排除社會民主黨。直接導火線發生在2月10日，聯邦警察在下奧地利的維也納新城解除共和國防護團武裝時發生流血衝突。政府隨後查封武器並解散社會民主黨青年組織，2月11日深夜至12日上午，維也納的黨武裝、產業工人與共和國防護團同時攻擊警察機關及軍械庫。因而，奪取武器、保衛已控制街區並阻止政府重新部署，成為起義最直接的軍事目的。
causeEn: The economic depression of 1933, rising unemployment, and wage cuts intensified the labor conflict. After the Social Democratic armed revolt of 1927 had been suppressed, the party was excluded from power, while its legal political activity and armed organization were restricted. Dollfuss's government gradually marginalized the Social Democrats by relying on the Christian Social movement, the federal police, and the Heimwehr. The immediate trigger occurred on 10 February, when federal police attempting to disarm members of the Republikanischer Schutzbund in Wiener Neustadt, Lower Austria, exchanged fire with them. The government then seized weapons and dissolved Social Democratic youth organizations. Between late hours on 11 February and the morning of 12 February, party militias, industrial workers, and Schutzbund members attacked police installations and military depots simultaneously. Obtaining arms, holding the districts already under their control, and preventing the government from redeploying therefore became the immediate military purposes of the uprising.
people: 政府方面，總理恩格爾貝特·多爾福斯以內閣身分協調警察、軍方與海姆韋爾，但並非前線指揮官；聯邦國防部長阿爾弗雷德·揚薩負責軍方部署，聯邦警察與海姆韋爾各單位則依任務自行行動。起義方面，前奧匈陸軍砲兵軍官朱利葉斯·德意志是最主要的武裝統籌者，他利用舊軍經驗把共和國防護團與維也納各區戰鬥員編成分區，負責奪取武器及維持外圍陣地。社會民主黨主席奧托·鮑爾是政治領導核心，負責與外地組織聯絡，但沒有直接指揮橋頭或街廓戰鬥。雙方都沒有把警察、軍事單位與武裝政黨整合成單一指揮系統，這使命令傳遞、彈藥分配與撤退安排在起義最激烈時仍不統一。
peopleEn: On the government side, Chancellor Engelbert Dollfuss coordinated the police, military, and Heimwehr through the cabinet rather than serving as a frontline commander. Federal Minister for Military Affairs Alfred Jansa directed the army's deployments, while federal police and Heimwehr units retained substantial independence in carrying out their assigned tasks. On the insurgent side, former Austro-Hungarian artillery officer Julius Deutsch was the principal military organizer. He used his previous military experience to divide the Schutzbund and Vienna's district fighters into separate formations responsible for taking weapons and holding positions on the outskirts. Social Democratic chairman Otto Bauer formed the political leadership and handled contact with provincial organizations, but he did not directly command fighting at the bridge or in the streets. Neither side combined its police, regular military units, and armed political organizations into a single command system, leaving orders, ammunition distribution, and withdrawal arrangements inconsistent at the height of the fighting.
kits: 聯邦陸軍的槍械以 Steyr-Mannlicher M1888/90、Mannlicher M1924/30 等步槍為主，警方及騎兵也保有 Karabiner M1892、Mannlicher M1895 卡賓槍，軍用手槍為 Steyr-Hahn M1914，通用機槍則是 Schwarzlose M. 07/12。政府把1927年列裝的7.5厘米 M.27 野戰榴彈砲用於支援步兵，並以少量1930年已列裝的 Steyr ADGZ 裝甲車執行道路機動與火力支援；1933年的聯邦陸軍沒有可供這場戰役使用的坦克部隊。起義者從警察分署、軍械庫及黨武裝手中取得上述槍械，但不同口徑與不同年代裝備混雜，其中8毫米 M1888/90 與7.92毫米 M1924/30 的彈藥不能互換。政府可沿鐵路把野戰砲、彈藥、燃料及野戰電話網送入中部兵營；起義者雖取得大量武器，卻只有零散彈藥和市內囤積，難以維持跨區持續補給。
kitsEn: The Federal Army's principal firearms included the Steyr-Mannlicher M1888/90 and Mannlicher M1924/30 rifles, while the police and cavalry retained the Karabiner M1892 and Mannlicher M1895 carbines. The standard military pistol was the Steyr-Hahn M1914, and the general-purpose machine gun was the Schwarzlose M. 07/12. The government employed the 7.5 cm M.27 field howitzer, fielded in 1927, to support infantry and used a small number of Steyr ADGZ armored cars, already in service by 1930, for road movement and fire support. The Austrian Federal Army had no operational tank force available for the fighting in 1933. The insurgents obtained these same weapons from police stations, military depots, and party arsenals, but their equipment mixed different calibers and generations of weapons. In particular, 8 mm M1888/90 ammunition and 7.92 mm M1924/30 ammunition were not interchangeable. The government could move field guns, ammunition, fuel, and field telephone networks into the central barracks by rail. The insurgents possessed many weapons but only scattered ammunition and urban stockpiles, making sustained supply across several fronts difficult.
tactics: 起義初期採取同時發動的小隊突襲。攻擊者在得手後沒有向內城中心作連續總攻，而是以法沃里滕、弗洛里茨多夫和普拉施－呂迪格橋為外圍支撐，在警察分署、路口與橋頭設置機槍陣位，利用現成街廓和障礙物分割政府軍推進路線。普拉施－呂迪格橋跨越多瑙運河，橋面與兩端街廓形成狹窄正面，起義者由橋頭側擊企圖過橋的步兵，政府軍則必須先肅清橋頭再由南岸逐段推進。政府沒有同時強攻所有外圍區域，而是先鞏固中央警察機關、軍械庫、廣播與交通線，再由阿森納、蘭德韋爾兵營及主要道路投入步兵，以 M.27 榴彈砲壓制固定陣位，裝甲車則在較寬道路上提供機動火力。起義者曾反覆嘗試支援橋頭與外圍各區，卻因命令、預備隊和彈藥調配不一致而難以形成連續攻勢。最後兩日，政府封鎖外圍通道，把砲兵逐段向前移，依次清除據點，使起義力量失去可互相掩護的地理條件。
tacticsEn: The insurgents initially used simultaneous attacks by small groups. After taking their objectives, they did not launch a continuous general assault toward the center of Vienna. Instead, they formed an outer framework around Favoriten, Floridsdorf, and the Prasch-Rüdiger-Steg, placing machine-gun positions at police stations, road junctions, and bridgeheads. Existing buildings and barricades divided the government's approach routes. The Prasch-Rüdiger-Steg crossed the Danube Canal, and its deck and the streets on either bank formed a narrow front. Insurgents fired on infantry attempting to cross from the bridgeheads, while government troops first had to clear the approaches before advancing from the south. The government did not assault every outer district simultaneously. It first secured the central police installations, the arsenal, broadcasting, and transport lines, then sent infantry from the Arsenal, the Landwehr barracks, and the main roads. M.27 field howitzers suppressed fixed positions, while armored cars provided mobile fire along the broader avenues. The insurgents repeatedly attempted to reinforce the bridgehead and outer districts, but inconsistent orders, reserves, and ammunition distribution prevented a sustained offensive. During the final two days, the government sealed the outward routes, moved artillery forward in sections, and cleared each strongpoint in turn, depriving the insurgents of the terrain that had allowed their positions to support one another.
data: 2月10日，聯邦警察在維也納新城解除共和國防護團武裝，交火使政府與黨武裝的對立公開化。2月11日深夜，維也納各區完成動員；2月12日上午，起義者向警察機關及阿森納軍械庫發動攻擊，取得步槍、機槍與彈藥，至傍晚已控制大半外圍市區，而內城核心、政府機關與數處主要兵營仍由聯邦陸軍守住。2月13日，政府軍從兵營反攻，奪回中央警察機關周邊並鞏固阿森納區；起義者退守法沃里滕、弗洛里茨多夫及多瑙運河上的普拉施－呂迪格橋。2月14日至15日，政府軍在法沃里滕軍營區、弗洛里茨多夫與橋頭反覆攻擊，外地礦區及鐵路據點則因無法與維也納主力建立聯絡而陸續受挫。2月16日，政府集中增援、機槍、裝甲車與榴彈砲，攻破部分外圍陣地；2月17日，最後一批據點被占，起義在省級支部尚能形成有效配合之前結束。
dataEn: On 10 February, federal police attempting to disarm the Republikanischer Schutzbund in Wiener Neustadt exchanged fire with its members, openly exposing the confrontation between the government and the party militia. Mobilization was completed across Vienna late on 11 February. On the morning of 12 February, the insurgents attacked police installations and the Vienna Arsenal, obtaining rifles, machine guns, and ammunition. By evening they controlled most of the outer city, while Federal Army troops still held the central city, government installations, and several principal barracks. On 13 February, government troops counterattacked from the barracks, retook the area around the central police headquarters, and consolidated the Arsenal district. The insurgents withdrew to Favoriten, Floridsdorf, and the Prasch-Rüdiger-Steg over the Danube Canal. From 14 to 15 February, government forces attacked repeatedly around the Favoriten barracks, Floridsdorf, and the bridgehead, while provincial mining and railway positions were defeated in succession because they could not establish contact with the main force in Vienna. On 16 February, the government concentrated reinforcements, machine guns, armored cars, and field howitzers against the outer positions. On 17 February, the last strongpoints were occupied, ending the uprising before its provincial organizations could be brought into effective coordination.
impact: 起義失敗的直接制度後果，是社會民主黨的武裝與合法組織能力遭到清除。共和國防護團被正式禁止，相關青年組織停止公開活動，黨報與部分工會活動受到更嚴格限制；1933年6月22日，社會民主黨本身也被政府宣布非法。這使多爾福斯得以把黨的軍事殘餘與政治存在分開處理，並加速推動以祖國陣線及職業代表制為核心的國家重組，雖說這場戰役本身不是1934年五月憲法的制憲程序，卻為其鋪平了道路。起義者失去再次迅速動員的武器網與外圍據點，社會民主黨的地方骨幹遭到重創，部分領導者被捕或流亡，海外組織則只能在遠離奧地利的條件下重建聯絡。與此同時，聯邦軍隊與海姆韋爾的武裝地位上升，但海姆韋爾的獨立傾向也成為多爾福斯政權新的內部約束。
impactEn: The immediate institutional consequence of the uprising's defeat was the destruction of the Social Democratic Party's armed and legal organization. The Republikanischer Schutzbund was formally prohibited, the related youth organizations ended their public activity, and restrictions on the party press and parts of union activity were tightened. On 22 June 1933, the Social Democratic Party itself was declared illegal by the government. This allowed Dollfuss to separate the party's military remnants from its political existence and accelerated the reconstruction of the state around the Fatherland Front and occupational representation. The uprising was not itself the constitutional process that produced the May Constitution of 1934, but it cleared the way for it. The insurgents lost both the weapons network needed for rapid remobilization and their peripheral strongpoints. The local backbone of the Social Democratic Party suffered severe damage, some leaders were arrested or went into exile, and the overseas organization could rebuild contacts only under conditions removed from Austria. At the same time, the standing of the Federal Army and the Heimwehr increased, although the Heimwehr's independent ambitions became a new internal constraint on Dollfuss's regime.
result: 2月17日，政府軍占據起義者最後的主要據點，維也納外圍的槍械與彈藥被重新查收，零散抵抗隨後失去協同而告終。這是一場政府方面的完整戰術勝利，也是起義方面最徹底的戰略失敗：政府從開戰起便掌握內城、鐵路、國家電台、火砲與集中部署能力，起義者雖以突襲奪取武器並一度控制廣大外圍地區，卻沒有把初勝轉化為跨區指揮、持續補給、反砲兵火力或能與省級組織接應的統一戰役。關於死亡，較常見的戰史整理把戰鬥及緊接其後鎮壓中的總數估為一百五十至二百人，但各來源對雙方歸屬、獄中死亡與後續處決的計法不同，因此只能採用這個估算區間，不能把任何單一總數或雙方分解視為確定值。
resultEn: On 17 February, government forces occupied the insurgents' last major strongpoints, the weapons and ammunition in the outer districts of Vienna were recovered, and the remaining resistance lost coordination and ended. This was a complete tactical victory for the government and a comprehensive strategic defeat for the insurgents. The government controlled the inner city, railways, state broadcasting, artillery, and centralized deployment from the beginning. Although the insurgents seized weapons by surprise and briefly controlled a large outer area, they could not convert that initial success into interdistrict command, sustained supply, counter-artillery fire, or a unified war capable of receiving support from provincial organizations. Regarding deaths, common historical compilations generally estimate the combined total during the fighting and the immediate repression at 150 to 200, but sources differ in assigning the dead, counting deaths in custody, and treating subsequent executions. The estimate can therefore only be retained as a range; neither a single total nor a precise breakdown between the two sides can be treated as certain.
